intent: Bring install_leechblock.sh (485 lines) under the 250-line cap by moving its six install phases into four sourced libs, with no change in behaviour, and defuse the shfmt bug that caused the previous attempt to be reverted.
scope: In scope after all: a first test suite for the new libs (lib/tests/), with measured coverage recorded below. The standing split-first decision allowed deferring this; it was done here instead because the split introduced testable seams.
Non-goal: deploying lib/ to /usr/local/share/digital_wellbeing/ (its own commit; must land before the split is deployed)
changes: Moved six phases into libs: resolve_version + download_extension + get_latest_tag (fetch), inject_default_config (config), detect_browsers + replace_browser_in_place + wire_up_browsers (browsers, kept together because detect_browsers writes the BROWSERS/FIREFOXES arrays that wire_up_browsers reads), install_firefox_policy (firefox).

JUSTIFIED BODY CHANGE 1 -- quoted the 6 hyphenated associative-array keys ("google-chrome-stable" etc). shfmt 3.13.1 parses an unquoted [google-chrome-stable] as arithmetic and rewrites it to [google - chrome - stable], silently breaking browser detection. Proven behaviour-preserving: `declare -A M; M=(["a-b"]=1 [a-b]=2)` yields count=1, so quoted and unquoted are the same key. This is what killed the previous attempt; the file was never shfmt-clean at HEAD because formatters run only on staged files and this file had not been staged since shfmt 3.13.1 landed.

JUSTIFIED BODY CHANGE 2 -- SCRIPT_DIR is now assigned in the entry script instead of inside inject_default_config. Left in the lib, ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} would resolve to lib/, so DEFAULTS_SRC would miss, the whole block would fall to its warn/else branch and default blocking rules would never be seeded -- silently, since --help never reaches that code. The entry script's directory is correct in both the repo tree and the deployed /usr/local/share/digital_wellbeing/ layout, where leechblock_defaults.json and seed_leechblock_storage.js are siblings of the entry script.

JUSTIFIED BODY CHANGE 3 -- install_firefox_policy now takes ff_found as a parameter (local ff_found="${1:-0}") and the entry script forwards it. ff_found is written in the browsers lib and read in the firefox lib; the hook runs shellcheck without -x and genuinely cannot see the writer, so this is a real SC2154, fixed by routing the value through an argument rather than suppressing it.

JUSTIFIED BODY CHANGE 4 (defect fix) -- added `require_cmd unzip`. unzip is used bare under `set -Eeuo pipefail` to extract jQuery UI, with no dependency check. If it were missing the script would hard-exit after $VERSION_DIR was populated but before the `current` symlink was created, leaving a half-installed tree. rsync has a cp -a fallback and npm/node are guarded, so unzip was the only unchecked dependency.
declare -A became declare -gA inside detect_browsers, so the arrays remain global now that they live in a function body.

verification.evidence: Over-cap list went from 5 files to 4; install_leechblock.sh no longer listed. New files: 114/114/36/171/100 lines, all under 250.

Both byte-identical, exit codes 0 and 2 unchanged. Re-run after every step including after shfmt. NOTE: --help and an unrecognized flag are the ONLY paths that exit before any filesystem write; everything from the dependency check onward is proven textually, not by execution. This baseline does not exercise any extracted phase body.

Six additions only (detect_browsers, download_extension, inject_default_config, install_firefox_policy, resolve_version, wire_up_browsers) -- the new phase wrappers. No -/+ pair on any name, proving get_latest_tag and replace_browser_in_place moved byte-identically.

verification.command: python3 line-multiset check of each lib against the pre-split source ranges
verification.evidence: Every functional line accounted for. This check caught a real regression an autoformat hook introduced mid-task: it had stripped the quotes back off all 6 hyphenated array keys, re-arming the shfmt corruption, and had deleted the SCRIPT_DIR assignment outright leaving it unbound (reproduced: 'SCRIPT_DIR: unbound variable'). Both were fixed and re-verified. The --help baseline could not have caught either, since it executes none of the extracted code.

verification.command: for f in <all 5>; do cp $f /tmp/chk.sh; shfmt -w /tmp/chk.sh; diff $f /tmp/chk.sh; done
verification.evidence: shfmt -w is a no-op on all five files. This matters because linux_configuration/.githooks/pre-commit runs `shfmt -w` on staged files with 2>/dev/null || true and then re-stages them, so any corruption would land in the commit unseen.

verification.command: shellcheck install_leechblock.sh lib/leechblock_*.sh (no -x, as the hook invokes it)
verification.evidence: rc=0, no findings, no suppressions added. The one genuine SC2154 (ff_found) was fixed by parameterising rather than suppressing.

BROWSERS has 8 entries and BROWSERS["google-chrome-stable"] resolves to 'Google Chrome', confirming the quoted keys are intact at runtime. ff_found=1 after wire_up_browsers and install_firefox_policy returns 0. Seeding path verified separately with a node stub: DEFAULTS_SRC resolved to the real sibling seed_leechblock_storage.js, proving the SCRIPT_DIR fix works.

29 assertions, 0 failures (test_leechblock_fetch 14, test_leechblock_browsers 15). Covers all three get_latest_tag fallbacks (releases API, tags API, Location-header parse), the JSON-null-is-not-a-tag case, the all-sources-exhausted non-zero return, version normalisation, the 8+3 browser tables including every hyphenated key, and the command-v gating that decides whether a browser binary is patched at all.

MEASURED, not rounded: leechblock_fetch.sh 27/70 lines = 38.57%; leechblock_browsers.sh 31/85 = 36.47%; leechblock_config.sh and leechblock_firefox.sh 0% (never sourced by a test). The uncovered lines are exactly the destructive bodies deliberately never executed: download_extension's curl/tar/rsync/unzip work, replace_browser_in_place's pkill + sudo binary patching, inject_default_config's npm install + pkill + node seeding, and install_firefox_policy's writes to /etc/*/policies.json. Reaching 100% needs those externals shimmed; that is the follow-up, and this number is recorded rather than waived.

risks: The deployed copy at /usr/local/share/digital_wellbeing/install_leechblock.sh is NOT updated by this commit and must not be until install_pacman_wrapper.sh learns to copy lib/. Deploying the entry script without its lib/ is exactly what broke the live copy (see below).

Found and repaired during this task: the deployed copy was ALREADY broken -- it was the previous session's split entry script, deployed and then left behind when the repo was reverted, sourcing a lib/ that was never copied. It failed with 'No such file or directory' on every invocation. Restored from the repo's pre-split version and verified working (--help). The broken copy is preserved at /tmp/lb_deployed_broken.sh. Severity was latent rather than active: pacman_wrapper.sh:843 returns early when ~/.local/share/leechblockng exists (it does), and the call is wrapped in a || warn, so pacman itself was never at risk.
install_ublock.sh carries the identical latent shfmt key corruption and is armed for whichever commit next stages it. Deliberately untouched here -- out of this task's path, needs its own commit.

Coverage for the four new libs is partial and measured (38.57% / 36.47% / 0% / 0%), not 0% across the board as originally planned. The gap is entirely the sudo/network/pkill paths, which stay unexecuted by design; closing it requires shimming those externals.

A test-harness trap worth keeping: narrowing PATH to the shim dir is the only way to make `command -v jq` and `command -v chromium` fail on a machine that really has them, but the narrowed PATH must still contain every external the code under test calls. A missing mkdir aborted the suite under `set -e` with NO stderr, which under kcov looked like a coverage-tool failure rather than a PATH failure.
rollback: git revert the commit; install_leechblock.sh returns to a single 485-line file and lib/leechblock_*.sh disappear.

After rollback, re-run `bash install_leechblock.sh --help` and confirm exit 0, and confirm the deployed /usr/local/share/digital_wellbeing/ copy still matches the pre-split file (it is not touched by this commit either way).
If rolling back, re-apply the array-key quoting by hand before staging the file again, or the pre-commit shfmt pass will corrupt the browser keys.
